title: Gavin Newsom Mocks 'Golden Age of Super Intelligence,' Calls President's 'Let It Rip' Approach to AI 'Reckless'
key_facts: California Governor Gavin Newsom posted on X on Wednesday 30 Sep 2026 that the White House's AI announcement was 'bullshit', comparing it to 'Big Pharma saying we don't need the FDA', and called Trump's 'let it rip' approach 'RECKLESS'.
In the clip he shared, Newsom compared AI oversight to rules for pharmaceuticals and airlines and said industries should not decide for themselves whether safeguards are needed.

He said California must accelerate its own AI regulation in the absence of federal leadership, and that an independent group set up by his executive order will review AI issues, with California to implement its recommendations.
Newsom also mocked the White House 'Accord on Super Intelligence' by sharing an image showing a spelling error ('Unites States') under Trump's signature.

The accord, also called a 'Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities', is a voluntary pact signed by Trump and the heads of Alphabet, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI (president Greg Brockman), xAI and Nvidia, calling for independent audits, stronger internal controls and board-level oversight.
Trump called the pact 'morally binding' and said companies should police their own AI development.
quote_evidence: "What we saw from the White House yesterday was bullshit," he wrote. "It's like Big Pharma saying we don't need the FDA. Donald Trump's 'let it rip' approach to AI is RECKLESS."
"We have to do a lot more in the absence of federal leadership, which they doubled down on yesterday," Newsom said.
Trump described the pact as "morally binding" and said companies should take responsibility for policing their own AI development.
why_it_matters_hint: The governor of the state where most AI labs sit says California will speed up its own rules because Washington has stepped back.
notes: Yahoo page carries Benzinga's text (copyright Benzinga); Benzinga is the source, Yahoo the copy site; the Benzinga URL was not shown, so url is the Yahoo page. Newsom's post was on Wednesday 30 Sep, several days before the window, re-published 4 Oct.
